passage: Mental health is about our emotional, psychological, and social well-being, which affects how we think, feel, and act. It is not the same as mental illness; everyone has mental health, just as everyone has physical health. Sometimes, people experience challenges like anxiety, which is a normal reaction to stress, such as before exams. While a little stress can help us focus, too much pressure can be harmful. If you feel overwhelmed, it is important to talk to a trusted adult, like a teacher, counselor, or family member, rather than keeping your worries inside. Anxiety can cause physical symptoms like a racing heart or stomach aches, showing that it affects the whole body, not just the mind. Mental illnesses are health conditions that can be managed or treated with professional support, just like physical illnesses. It is a myth that mental illness is caused by curses or bad deeds; it is a medical reality. Also, remember that your marks do not define your worth as a person. If you or a friend are struggling, seeking help is a sign of strength, and many helplines offer free, confidential support for students. Taking short breaks during study sessions actually helps your brain perform better, so it is never a waste of time.

items.evidence: While a little stress can help us focus, too much pressure can be harmful.
items.q: Meera feels a little nervous before a test and it helps her focus. What does this show?
options: Mild stress can be useful, though too much harms
All stress is harmful and must be avoided
More pressure always means better marks in exams
Feeling nervous means she has a mental illness
items.explain: A little stress can help us focus, but too much pressure can be harmful.

wrong.why: thinks more pressure always improves performance

items.evidence: If you feel overwhelmed, it is important to talk to a trusted adult, like a teacher, counselor, or family member, rather than keeping your worries inside.
items.q: Why is it better to share a heavy worry with a trusted adult?
options: They can support you before it grows bigger
Worries vanish once you stop thinking of them
Only girls are meant to share their feelings
Sharing shows you are weak and cannot cope
items.explain: When overwhelmed, talking to a trusted adult helps, rather than keeping worries inside.

wrong.why: thinks hiding worries makes them vanish
thinks showing feelings is only for girls
thinks asking for help shows weakness

items.evidence: Anxiety can cause physical symptoms like a racing heart or stomach aches, showing that it affects the whole body, not just the mind.
items.q: Which example shows that anxiety affects the body, not only the mind?
options: A student gets a stomach ache before a test
A student feels sad after losing a game
A student cannot stop thinking about homework
A student feels angry when teased by friends
items.explain: Anxiety can cause body symptoms like a racing heart or stomach aches, so it affects the whole body.

wrong.why: thinks feelings like sadness are the physical sign
thinks anxiety stays only in the mind
picks another emotion that is not a body symptom

items.evidence: Also, remember that your marks do not define your worth as a person.
items.q: Karan scores low marks in a test. What does this say about his worth?
options: Nothing, as marks do not decide a person's value
It shows he is less valuable than toppers
It shows he should study without any breaks
It shows he must hide his feelings from everyone
items.explain: Marks do not define worth as a person, so a low score does not lower his value.

wrong.why: thinks feelings should be kept inside

items.evidence: Mental illnesses are health conditions that can be managed or treated with professional support, just like physical illnesses.
items.q: Why is treatment worth trying for a person with a mental illness?
options: Such conditions can be managed with expert help
Such conditions are never cured, so help is useless
Such conditions are a sign of a weak character
Such conditions make a person dangerous to others
items.explain: Mental illnesses can be managed or treated with professional support, like physical illnesses.

wrong.why: thinks mental illness is a character flaw
thinks people with mental illness are dangerous
